newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, Arabs spar over burning of Israeli flag.
newsitem.headline: Israel, Arabs spar over burning of Israeli flag.

text.p: Palestinian Legislative Council Speaker Ahmed Korei on Sunday brushed aside Israeli criticism of his presence at the burning of an Israeli flag during a West Bank protest.
But Korei, who helped negotiate the PLO's breakthrough 1993 peace deal with Israel, denied trampling on the flag.

"I did not step on the flag. The burning of the flag during the demonstration was not planned. It was a surprise for me," said Korei, who led a 1,000-strong protest march on Saturday in Ramallah against expanding Jewish settlements.

"Yet if I thought that the burning of the flag would solve the problem, I would have burnt it with my own hands. But it doesn't. Our problem with Israel is the land, not the flag," Korei, known as Abu Ala, told Reuters.
"They want to divert the issue from one of occupation to that of a flag," he said.
Israeli Cabinet Secretary Danny Naveh told Israel Radio that for peace talks to resume, the Palestinian leadership would have to distance itself from acts of violence.
"Abu Ala marched at the head of a procession of demonstrators opposite whom an Israeli flag was burned. He didn't try to protest, he didn't try to stop it," Naveh said.
"He says he didn't walk on it. He walked 20 cms (8 inches) from the flag," Naveh said.

Israeli-Palestinian talks on the handover of more West Bank land to self-rule have been in crisis since Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu broke ground on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem four months ago.
The climate has given rise to accusations by both sides of hateful acts.

The West Bank town of Hebron has been a scene of almost daily unrest for more than two weeks since a Jewish woman put up posters depicting Islam's Prophet Mohammad as a pig. Israel apologised for the incident and the woman has been charged.
